pĕtăsĭo and pĕtăso , ōnis, m., = πετασών,
I.a leg or pestle of pork, esp. the shoulder (opp. perna, the ham): “e Galliā apportantur Romam pernae tomacinae et taniacae, et petasiones,” Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 10 : “pulpam dubio de petasone voras,” i. e. that has already begun to turn, Mart. 3, 77, 6 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
